CourseName: CEN3722 - Introduction to Human Computer Interfaces

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: This artifact outlines the module's topic structure, covering Figma fundamentals such as the interface, frames, grids, component libraries, and auto-layout, serving as a syllabus-style roadmap for learners and instructors to navigate the module's content sequence.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: An HTML page listing and briefly describing all topics covered in the module — including the Figma interface, tools, file organisation, and the end-to-end prototyping workflow — giving learners and instructors a structured overview of what the module contains.

Artifacts.Name: Creating_a_Prototype.pptx
Artifacts.Description: A slide deck walking learners step by step through building interactive prototypes in Figma, from setting up a free account and understanding fidelity levels to progressing from low- to high-fidelity designs, intended for use as a lecture presentation or self-study reference.

Artifacts.Name: Introduction to Figma and the Prototyping Workflow
Artifacts.Description: Introduces Figma's browser-based environment, core concepts, and overall prototyping workflow, giving learners foundational context before they begin working with the tool's specific features.

Artifacts.Name: Frames, Grids, and Screen Layout
Artifacts.Description: Explains how to use Figma frames as structural containers for digital interfaces and covers how grids and layout guides help designers create consistent, well-organized screen layouts.

Artifacts.Name: Building a Component Library
Artifacts.Description: Covers how to create, organize, and reuse components in Figma — including master components and instances — so learners can build a scalable design system that stays consistent across an entire project.

Artifacts.Name: Auto-Layout for Responsive Elements
Artifacts.Description: Explains Figma's auto-layout feature, showing learners how to build frames and components that automatically resize and reflow their contents when text changes or elements are added or removed.

Artifacts.Name: Interactive Prototyping and Connections
Artifacts.Description: Guides learners through wiring static frames into a clickable prototype using Figma's Prototype tab, including setting up connections, triggers, actions, transitions, and scrolling behaviors.

Artifacts.Name: High-Fidelity Design and Visual Polish
Artifacts.Description: Covers the techniques used to elevate wireframes into polished, high-fidelity mockups, focusing on visual properties such as typography, color, imagery, and other design details that reflect a realistic final product.

Artifacts.Name: Building and Submitting the Group Project Prototype
Artifacts.Description: Provides guidance on planning, collaborating, reviewing, and correctly submitting a group Figma prototype, helping student teams coordinate their work and meet submission requirements.

Artifacts.Name: Building and Submitting the Group Project Prototype
Artifacts.Description: Provides guidance on planning, collaborating, reviewing, and correctly submitting a group Figma prototype, helping student teams coordinate their work and meet submission requirements.

Artifacts.Name: ai_assisted_design_figma_prototype
Artifacts.Description: This group project artifact guides student teams through Phase 4 of a semester-long design sequence, tasking them with building an AI-assisted interface prototype in Figma that builds on their prior task analysis work, with an estimated team effort of 2–4 hours.
